top_choice_rationale: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling is a settled game-changer: bulky, electron-rich ligand design made C-N reductive elimination from Pd-amido complexes fast, giving aryl amines as a routine reaction, with decades of independent confirmation and a clean two-name allocation (Buchwald, Hartwig) within the three-laureate limit. Kosugi's tin-amide work was stoichiometric and narrow, and the citation can state C-N bond formation and ligand control to separate it from the 2010 C-C prize. Targeted protein degradation (P003 over P004, since Ciulli's structure-based degrader design is the stronger chemistry case than the cereblon target identification) is a real new principle but lacks an approved degrader and has split credit; condensates (P002) are conceptually new but their physiological scope and credit are unsettled; no award ranks last.
